name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 33 points and Aderholt has held the seat since 1997
Challenger raised about $16,000 with $396 on hand versus Aderholt's $750,000
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 1%
No public general-election polling and no expert ratings flag the race
model.rationale: Aderholt's quarter-century incumbency in an R+33 district, paired with a roughly 65-to-1 fundraising advantage, leaves the Democratic nominee without a visible path, and markets price her chances near 1%. The only real question is the size of the margin, which the deep partisan lean suggests will be a large Republican win.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or a sudden influx of outside spending for the challenger would put the result in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 4th district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Robert Aderholt has held it since 1997. He is seeking another term with an overwhelming financial edge: about $1.0 million raised and $750,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek has raised roughly $16,000 and reported under $500 in the bank. No public general-election polls are available, and no major expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats about a 1% chance of an upset. The district's 33-point Republican lean, combined with incumbency and the fundraising gap, makes a competitive race highly unlikely. The main open question is the size of the winning margin rather than the winner, and every piece of available evidence points to a safely Republican seat.
